name: Beare

attributes.attribute: Irish goddess who gave name to the Beare peninsula
said to have been a Spanish princess
pre-Celtic land goddess known as the Hag of Beare
visible as a boulder looking toward the sea

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text:
Beare is an Irish goddess. She gave her name to a peninsula in the far southwest of Ireland. The land lies in the province of Munster. The thin Beare peninsula stretches out to sea. It is rich in both antiquities and legend.

Beare is also called Bera, Béirre, or Moméa. Little of her own legend survives. She is said to have been a Spanish princess. The greater fame belongs to the Cailleach Bhéirre, the Hag of Beare. She was an ancient land goddess of the pre-Celtic people.

The Hag stays bound to the peninsula. A boulder in her shape looks toward the sea from the north side. In some tellings the consonants shift. Then her name becomes Moméa.

okr.objective: Portray Beare as the goddess behind the Beare peninsula and its Hag of Beare tradition.
key_results: The Beare peninsula in Munster takes its name from the goddess.
Little legend of Beare survives; she is said to have been a Spanish princess.
The Cailleach Bhéirre, or Hag of Beare, was a pre-Celtic land goddess.
A boulder in the Hag's shape looks toward the sea on the north side.
